status: INFERENCE + RECOVERY ONLY. No training, no fine-tuning, no checkpoint modified, no architecture/generator/codec/recovery-algorithm change.
design_note: SALSA trains one model per secret. A frozen checkpoint encodes the secret it was trained on, so probing it always returns that secret. Experiment 1, the specified design, therefore cannot test generalisation across secrets and is reported as a secret-specificity control. Experiment 2 uses the three existing checkpoints, which were trained under different seeds and therefore on different secrets, and is the genuine test. It covers three secrets, not ten, because only three checkpoints exist and training more is out of scope.

experiment_1_secret_specificity_control.design: one frozen model, ten nominated fresh secrets
experiment_1_secret_specificity_control.what_it_measures: secret-specificity, NOT recovery robustness. The model encodes the secret it was trained on, and the recovery rule sees no secret, so the candidate cannot depend on which secret is nominated.

experiment_2_multi_secret_robustness.design: three checkpoints trained under different seeds, each attacked with its own secret; no training, existing checkpoints only
experiment_2_multi_secret_robustness.what_it_measures: whether recovery works for more than one secret

classification_text: exact recovery with independent verification on every secret tested
